subject: Draft: dedicated reservation, scaling & fallback agreement
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Rashid Khan <rashid.khan@medsilo.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated reservation: initial qualification and next steps

Rashid — thanks again for the time on today’s call. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth.

Summary of pain points you shared:
- Unpredictable latency at daily peak (batch workloads spike followed by latency cliffs).
- Multi-tenant "noisy neighbor" incidents causing servicing variance and throttled throughput.
- Compliance: data isolation and customer-segregated logs required for audits.
- Procurement timeline: 30–60 days with a preference for a fixed monthly commit.

Proposed dedicated-reservation approach (high level):
- Reserved pool: start with an 8-GPU A100 pool (2 nodes x 4 GPUs) for phase 1 pilot.
- Isolation: dedicated tenant + VPC peering; KMS-backed encryption for at-rest model assets and KV cache.
- Scaling & fallback: primary pool handles steady traffic; burst policy uses shared burst capacity for short windows, with automated graceful fallback to a quantized / smaller model if we hit pool saturation (keeps tail latency bounded).
- SLO targets to validate in pilot: p95 latency < 300ms for generative endpoints; sustained throughput target ~200 reqs/sec with cold-starts < 250ms after warm-up.

Preliminary commercial assumptions (ballpark to align expectations):
- Reserved 12-month commit estimate attached (see proposal-medSilo-12m.csv).
- Option for a 2-week pilot with billing credit toward committed term if you convert.

Attachments sent with this note: medsilo-map-20260912.xlsx (MOP + test plan), redwood-sla-draft-20260912.pdf (SLA draft).

Next steps / asks (owner):
1) Sean/GTM: Send detailed proposer and SLA draft (attached) — DONE.
2) Monica/SE: Share pilot MOP and load test checklist (attached).
3) Rashid: Confirm procurement window and security checklist items you want us to prioritize (e.g., SOC2 evidence, KMS/HSM requirements).
4) Align pilot kickoff: propose week of Sep 21 for a 2-week pilot — please confirm availability.

If agreeable, I can convert the SLA draft into a redline-ready Google Doc and loop in your procurement contact. Thanks — appreciate the clarity on priorities today.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0199

Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 17:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated reservation: initial qualification and next steps

Thanks Sean — solid recap, appreciate the clarity. A couple clarifying items from our side before we share with procurement: 

1) Encryption & keys: we need confirmation you support customer-managed keys (bring-your-own KMS) and HSM-backed key storage. Can you confirm specifics for both model artifacts and runtime KV cache?
2) Audit evidence: procurement will want a SOC 2 Type II report plus any pen-test summary you can share. Do you have those ready?
3) Pilot scope: for the 2-week pilot, we want to run the following tests: burst load for 10–15m windows (3x baseline), model-switch fallback behavior, and simulating noisy neighbor scenarios. Your MOP checklist looks fine but we’ll want defined acceptance criteria.
4) Commercial: can you provide a 12-month committed price vs. month-to-month pricing? If we commit for 12 months we expect a material discount and priority for burst capacity.

If we can get the KMS/HSM confirmation and SOC2 artifacts, I’ll loop in our procurement lead (Ellen Park) and propose internal times to kick off the pilot. Otherwise the timeline slips.

—Rashid
Rashid Khan
Head of Platform Engineering, MedSilo Health
rashid.khan@medsilo.com

Rashid — thanks for the questions. Quick answers and an updated attachment (proposal-medSilo-12m.csv) with a 12-month committed option and a month-to-month comparator.

1) KMS/HSM: we support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS / GCP KMS / Azure Key Vault; for customers requiring HSM-backed keys we integrate with BYO-HSM via a supported KMIP bridge. This covers model artifacts at rest, KV cache encryption keys, and encryption for snapshot exports. We’ll provide the implementation note for your security team.

2) SOC2 & security artifacts: attaching a link in related_links to our latest SOC2 Type II summary and a one-page pen-test highlights doc. If you need full reports under NDA, we can provision them to procurement.

3) Pilot acceptance criteria (proposal excerpt):
- Functional: generate baseline throughput at 200 reqs/sec for primary model for 30 continuous minutes.
- Resilience: during a 15-minute burst (3x baseline), failover to quantized fallback model with <2% error rate and p95 latency < 500ms.
- Isolation: no cross-tenant KV cache leakage; per-tenant audit logs validated.

4) Commercial: the attached CSV includes a 12-month committed price with a 22% discount vs month-to-month and a clause for burst priority. We’re happy to fold an explicit credit for pilot costs into the committed term if you convert.

Next actions from us (short list):
- Monica to run through the MOP and add concrete test commands and metrics (she’s already started that doc).
- I’ll prepare a redline-ready SLA doc if you want to start procurement review.
- If OK, we’ll target Sep 21 kickoff for the pilot and confirm exact test windows.

I’ll also drop the SOC2 / pen-test links into the HubSpot deal and share the Drive folder with Ellen once you confirm procurement contact.

—Sean

Ellen, we’ll need the SOC2 and pen-test artifacts for procurement; Sean, please route those to Ellen via the Drive link / HubSpot record. Also please include the MOP checklist with explicit commands and expected thresholds so our infra team can run the automation.

I’ll get back with final confirmation on Friday after procurement sync. Thanks all.

—Rashid
